header: Stereo. H C J D A 38
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE.
body: Date of hearing: 25.11.2026 Appellants by: Mr. Qamar Zaman Qureshi, Additional Advocate General, Punjab.
Respondent No. 1: Ammara Hamid, in person.

Respondent No. 2: Unrepresented MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR, J. The appellants through this Intra Court Appeal filed under Section 3 of the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972 seek setting aside the order dated 15.03.2019 (‘impugned order’) passed by learned Single Judge of this Court, who allowed Writ Petition No. 65025 of 2017 filed by respondent No.1 and set aside the order dated 23.08.2017, whereby the letter dated 30.07.2017 appointing respondent No.1 as ESE (Sci-Math) in BPS-09 had been cancelled and directed the appellant No.1 to reinstate the respondent No.1 in service.

2. Learned Law Officer appearing on behalf of the appellants maintains that although the order dated 15.03.2019 passed in W.P. No. 65025 of 2017 had been implemented by the appellant/authority but letter of agreement dated 13.10.2020 (‘appointment letter’) was issued to respondent No.1 subject to final decision of this appeal. Further states that the impugned order is not sustainable as the same has been passed against the law settled in previous judgments of this Court and to strengthen his stance has referred to judgment dated 06.04.2023 passed in ICA No.56780 of 2020.

3. On the other hand, respondent No.1, who is present in person, states that she after being reinstated in service has also been regularized in service, hence the case of the appellants is distinguishable on facts from the above-mentioned judgment referred to by the learned Law Officer representing the appellants. It is further claimed that despite the pendency for last more than seven years, the appellants did not pursue the titled appeal diligently as they never made any attempt to have the same fixed, argued or decided at the earliest, and in the meanwhile a vested right has been created in favour of respondent No.1 to continue her services as her services had been regularized and appreciated by competent authority through various certificates, therefore this appeal has become infructuous. Besides it is also claimed that the appeal is barred by time and is liable to be dismissed on the said account as well.

4. Although various grounds pro and contra have been raised by both the parties, yet as the question of the titled appeal having been filed within prescribed period of limitation is involved, this Court in terms of Section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908 (“Act”) is required to address the said issue, even if it had not been raised, before proceeding further with the matter. In this regard, reliance may be placed on the judgment reported as Province of Sindh through Land Acquisition Officer versus Abdul Tawab and others (PLD 2026 SC 113), wherein it has been laid down that it is the inherent duty of the Court to delve into the question of limitation on its own, regardless of whether it is raised or not.

5. Perusal of the record shows that the impugned order was passed on 15.03.2019 and the Intra Court Appeal in terms of Article 151 of the Act was required to be filed within 20 days of passing of the said order, which were to expire on 04.04.2019, beyond which date the same would be barred by limitation. Reliance may be placed on Government of the Punjab through Chief Secretary Punjab, Lahore and another versus Muhammad Ibrahim Azad (1998 CLC 569 Lahore), Abdul Majeed and 2 others versus Federation of Pakistan through Secretary to Government of Pakistan and 8 others (PLD 2012 Lahore 112) and Province of Punjab and others versus Aftab Ahmad (2012 PLC (CS) 1402 Lahore).

6. Although the appeal was filed on 04.04.2019, which was the last date for filing the appeal and received by the office of this Court vide Diary No.54263 of 2019, yet it was totally incomplete and objection to that effect was raised by the office through entry No.43 of the objection sheet. The appellants were required to file complete appeal within the period of limitation and in case any objection is raised by the office, they were required to refile the same by removing the objection within period of limitation prescribed by law, otherwise the same on that account would become barred by limitation. Reliance may be placed on Asad Ali and 9 others versus The Bank of Punjab and others (PLD 2020 SC 736) and Muhammad Faisal, Proprietor, F.A. Traders, Lahore versus Commissioner Inland Revenue, Zone-II, RTO-II, Lahore (2025 SCMR 930), wherein by placing reliance upon aforementioned case of Asad Ali, it has been held that if objections raised by the office of the Court were not removed within the time specified by the office and in the meantime limitation for filing appeal stands expired, the appeal would be rendered time barred.

7. It would be pertinent to mention here that the appellants refiled the appeal on 14.05.2019 vide diary No.29531 of 2019 but by that time the appeal had become time barred by 40 days. It is settled by now that the appellants were required to refile the appeal after removing office objection within the limitation period and if the appeal is refiled after limitation period has expired, each and every day of delay is required to be explained by filing an application under Section 5 of the Act, wherein the appellants were required to provide sufficient cause for not filing or refiling the appeal with the prescribed time. Reliance is placed on MCB Bank Limited versus Uzma Tehreem and others (2026 SCMR 533).

8. Even if by virtue of Section 12 of the Act, the time requisite for obtaining certified copy of impugned order is excluded i.e., 12 days in total, between 15.03.2019, when application for obtaining certified copy was filed and 26.03.2019, when the same was prepared, the appeal still remains barred by 28 days. Although the appellants were required to file an application for condoning the delay in filing the titled appeal, till today no such attempt has been made to file any application under Section 5 of the Act, to seek condoning of delay, which is fatal to their case in terms of principles laid down in Iftikhar Ahmad versus Mst. Jehan Ara and 3 others (2007 SCMR 449) and Ahmad Jan and others versus Qazi Azizul Haq and others (2009 SCMR 1022), wherein in the latter judgment while considering a case of belatedly filed review application the Supreme Court has held that as the respondent did not file application under Section 5 of the Act for condonation of delay in filing of review petition thus, the High Court has erred in entertaining the review petition.

9. Moreover, the principles of limitation are applicable to all parties equally and the government cannot claim preferential treatment or claim that limitation was not strictly applicable to it. Reliance is placed on Province of Sindh through Land Acquisition Officer versus Abdul Tawab and others (PLD 2026 SC 113), wherein it is provided that the doctrine of equality before law demanded that all litigants, including the State, were accorded the same treatment and the law was administered in an even-handed manner and carelessness, intentional or obvious sluggishness, or dearth of bona fide were no reason for condonation of delay.

10. The appellants should have been vigilant in pursuing the remedy and should have filed the appeal within time or while refiling the same after removal of office objection sought condoning of delay by providing sufficient cause for the delay, which has not been done. It is a settled principle of law, reiterated by various Courts including in the case of Abdul Tawab (supra), Rehmat Din and others versus Mirza Nasir Abbas and others (2007 SCMR 1560) and Lahore Development Authority versus Mst. Sharifan Bibi and another (PLD 2010 SC 705) that law favours the vigilant and not the indolent.

11. It is also pertinent to mention here that law of limitation is not a mere technical rule of procedure, but it is founded upon sound public policy aimed at securing certainty, finality and repose in litigation. Once a valuable right accrues to a successful litigant by efflux of time, such right cannot be disturbed except upon demonstration of sufficient cause within the contemplation of law. Equally settled is the principle that a party seeking condonation of delay must approach the Court with clean hands, disclose all material facts and furnish a plausible, satisfactory and bona fide explanation covering the entire period of delay and negligence, indolence or casual conduct does not constitute sufficient cause. These principles have been borrowed and derived from the judgment reported as Muhammad Jahangir and others versus Haji Muhammad Ashraf (2026 SCMR 1995).

12. Moreover, it has been held in Capital Development Authority (CDA), through Chairman, Islamabad and others versus Dr. Sheikh Muhammad Shoaib Shafi and another (2026 SCMR 1033) that law of limitation results in extinguishment of a right of a party when significant lapses occur and no sufficient cause for such lapses, delay or time-barred action is shown by the defaulting party; the opposite party becomes entitled to a right accrued by such lapses, hence, in view of the principles discussed above, a vested right has been created in favour of the respondent No.1 due to indolence of the appellants in failing to refile the appeal within time or seek condoning of delay by filing an application showing sufficient cause, which has matured by efflux of time and on that account, this appeal being hopelessly barred by limitation is not proceedable and is liable to be dismissed and in view thereof no useful purpose would be served to discuss the other grounds raised in this appeal on behalf of either side.
13. For what has been discussed above, this appeal being hopelessly barred by limitation is accordingly dismissed.
JUDGE JUDGE Naveed * APPROVED FOR REPORTING
